title: Why I diversify: running multiple bootstrapped businesses to cut risk and keep momentum
summary: Damon Chen explains why he runs several bootstrapped businesses (Testimonial.to, PDF.ai, acquisitions) instead of going all in on one. Diversifying spreads risk, creates stable income, widens learning, avoids burnout and softens the exit-void after selling.

principles.text: Treat businesses like a stock portfolio: spread risk instead of relying on one business.
principles.quote: you don't put all your money in one stock you spread it out that way you know if one stock didn't go really well the others can make it up I think the same deal for business

principles.text: Bootstrappers building for their families need stable income, which multiple businesses provide better than one moonshot.
principles.quote: it is pretty important for Boost rappers because you know we mainly build our businesses for ourselves for our families so that's why we need the stable income

principles.text: Odds of a single business reaching unicorn/IPO are low, so don't plan around it.
principles.quote: I would say the chance of that happening is pretty low so let's just forget about it

principles.text: Running both B2B and B2C products lets you tap different markets and keep learning.
principles.quote: by having multiple businesses I get a chance to tap into different markets it's just fun to play in between B2B and b2c

principles.text: Staying open to new opportunities keeps you learning; each new business teaches new lessons (e.g. acquiring an AI product).
principles.quote: if you are open to any new opportunities the learning will never stop each business is a new adventure it has its own set of lessons

principles.text: Treat each new opportunity as another dart to throw; more darts raise the odds of success.
principles.quote: if every new opportunity gives me a new dart to throw I can keep collecting new darts and it will eventually increase the chance of getting the success
